video_caption: The video opens with a man in a red t-shirt walking and talking to the camera on a bustling street, with Japanese storefronts like "au" and "docomo" visible in the background, along with a "7-ELEVEN" sign. The scene then transitions to a closer shot of the 7-ELEVEN sign, displaying its iconic green, red, and orange logo. The video then quickly shifts to a couple, the man now in a light blue striped shirt and the woman with dark braids, sitting affectionately on a porch swing, with the partial text "It's" overlaid on the screen. This is followed by a shot of the same couple happily sitting on a couch with three young children, two of whom are holding plush toys, with the text "Life" visible, suggesting the title "It's Life". The woman is then shown in a close-up, smiling at the camera in front of a wooden wall. The scene transitions to a child in blue and white owl-patterned pajamas standing in a grey portable crib, followed by another shot of a child in colorful candy-patterned pajamas falling backwards in the crib before standing up. The man, shirtless, is then seen on a bed, holding and kissing a child in blue owl pajamas. The video moves to a kitchen counter displaying breakfast items: a frying pan, a mug, a glass with raw eggs, a pack of eggs, and a colorful package of "furikake" (Japanese rice seasoning) featuring cartoon girls. A hand picks up an individual furikake packet from the box. Next, a child in candy-patterned pajamas is shown picking an orange furikake packet from the box held by an unseen adult, while another child in blue owl pajamas walks in the background. The apartment's living/dining area is then shown, with the child in candy pajamas visible on a white bench. The two children are then seen sitting on the floor, playing with the furikake packets. Finally, the child in blue owl pajamas is shown on the floor, seemingly feeding her stuffed animals with the furikake packets. The video concludes with two children sitting at a wooden table, eating their breakfast, in the bright apartment living area, with large windows overlooking an outdoor courtyard.

A man in a red t-shirt walks along a busy urban street, talking to the camera, with buildings, a passing bus, and other vehicles in the background. The scene cuts to an exterior shot of a "7 ELEVEN" convenience store, easily recognizable by its distinctive red, green, and white striped logo above the entrance. The video then transitions back to the man as he enters the well-lit convenience store, continuing to speak while looking around at the merchandise. He approaches a shelf filled with various small bottles and packages, where he picks up a travel-sized, white and red package labeled "KEWPIE" (Kewpie), remarking on its cuteness. Below the shelf are price tags, one showing "¥93" and another "¥133." He points out other small items on the shelf, including bottles with yellow caps (likely soy sauce or oil) and red-capped containers (appearing to be spices or seasonings), stating he intends to buy these as gifts.

A person's hand reaches into a refrigerated display case in what appears to be a convenience store, first selecting a clear plastic cup of fruit jelly with a white lid featuring a peach illustration. The lid has Japanese text, "くだものゼリー 桃" (Kudamono Jelly Momo - Fruit Jelly Peach), and the cup is revealed to contain diced peaches. The price tag below reads "¥189 (税込 ¥204)" (including tax ¥204). The scene then shifts to a shelf stocked with Pocky boxes, where the hand picks up a gold box labeled "POCKY DEMITASSE" (ポッキー デミタス), displaying fancy chocolate-covered biscuit sticks. The price for this item is "¥121 (税込 ¥130)" (including tax ¥130). Next, the hand moves to a shelf of chocolate bars, picking up a brown box labeled "meiji chocolate" (meiji チョコレート) which appears to be a standard chocolate bar. Other varieties like "BLACK chocolate," "meiji Meltykiss" (meiji メルティーキッス), and "Strawberry" (ストロベリー) are visible, with prices like "¥114" and "¥132 (税込)" (including tax). Finally, the hand reaches into a freezer bin filled with numerous pre-packaged soft-serve ice cream cones, picking up one that is white and brown, clearly labeled with "7 ELEVEN" and "ミルクバニラ" (Milk Vanilla).

The video opens in a Japanese convenience store, focusing on a shelf displaying clear plastic jars with yellow lids filled with light brown, stringy dried squid, which a man's hand briefly picks up. The scene transitions to a different aisle featuring men's apparel, with packaged neckties (labeled "MEN'S NECKTIE" / ネクタイ, priced at ¥1300) and underwear/shirts (labeled "FEEL COTTON" and priced around ¥598) neatly arranged on shelves; a hand points to a necktie and then selects a black "FEEL COTTON" package. Above these, various hair styling products with images of young Japanese men showcase different styles like "AIR RISE" (エア感) and "GRUNGE MAT" (マット), as well as "Styling Grease." The camera then sweeps across a long aisle abundantly stocked with numerous varieties of instant cup and bowl noodles. Further down, small rectangular cartons of sake are visible, some dark blue with text like "かみなり" (Kaminari) and "180ml" (priced at ¥96), and others in white and red packaging. Adjacent to these are glass jars of sake labeled "まる" (Maru) and "200ml" (priced at ¥170), one of which a hand picks up. Next, a small, clear plastic container of "合鴨スモーク" (Aigamo Smoke - Smoked Duck, 70g) with "Pato ahumado" in Spanish is shown, which the hand confirms is "bacon in a can." Finally, the video highlights a vast selection of gummy candies, particularly focusing on red and blue bags of "GUMMI ColaUp" (コーラアップ), priced at ¥189. A man in a red t-shirt then appears, holding a bag of "ColaUp" gummies, expressing his fondness for them and describing their fizzy, Coca-Cola-like taste from his childhood. The segment concludes with a pan over the extensive array of Japanese gummies, including brands like "SOURS" and others, as the man voices his anticipation of missing them.

The video opens with a close-up of a light-skinned hand holding a red plastic cup with a gold lid, labeled "EMIAL タピオカミルクティー" (Tapioca Milk Tea). The cup features an image of tapioca pearls and a bubble tea graphic, and a thin, light-colored straw is attached to its side. On the shelf behind, several identical red cups are visible, along with white cups with blue lids (likely yogurt) and green-lidded cups, all bearing the 7-Eleven logo. A price tag below the bubble tea indicates "タピオカミルクティー" (Tapioca Milk Tea) and "¥221 (税込¥238)". The scene then transitions to a male with short dark hair, wearing a red shirt, holding the same bubble tea cup and looking directly at the camera, with the blurry convenience store interior as the background. Next, the camera pans across a refrigerated shelf in the store, showcasing various packaged fish items, including one labeled "さんまの塩焼き" (Grilled Saury with Salt) priced at "¥165" and another for "あじの南蛮漬け" (Aji no Nanbanzuke - marinated fried horse mackerel), all carrying the 7-Eleven brand. The final shot is another pan across a different section of the refrigerated shelf, displaying other packaged prepared meals such as "蒸し鶏とたっぷり野菜のサラダ" (Steamed Chicken and Plenty of Vegetable Salad) and "若鶏の炭火焼" (Charcoal-grilled Young Chicken), priced at "¥198 (税込¥213)", also with 7-Eleven branding.

A man in a red t-shirt stands in a brightly lit supermarket aisle, filled with shelves of various packaged snacks. He reaches out and picks up a clear plastic bag containing irregularly shaped, dark brown rice crackers. He holds the bag up to the camera, displaying its white and clear packaging with Japanese text and a prominent red circular label that reads "醤油" (Shoyu), meaning "soy sauce". He describes the snack as a very salty, soy sauce-flavored rice cracker, noting that it might also contain tamarind or soy sauce and has "extra flavor." He then points to another package on the shelf with a visible price tag of "148円" (148 yen) and "159円" (159 yen), likely indicating a regular and tax-inclusive price, and text that includes "8枚入" (8-mai iri), meaning "8 pieces included," and possibly "堅焼きこだわりしょうゆ" (Katayaki Kodawari Shoyu), meaning "Hard-baked specialty soy sauce." Next, he points to a red-packaged snack nearby, which likely features "とうがらし" (togarashi), or chili pepper, suggesting a spicy flavor, mentioning that while some of these snacks are available in Seattle, this specific one is not.

The video opens with a hand opening a white box to reveal a clear plastic-wrapped item containing three rectangular pieces of food, possibly sandwiches or pastries, with a dark filling, and a white packet labeled with Japanese characters「まい泉」(Maisen), referring to the brand. The wrapper on the food also clearly shows "MAISEN" printed repeatedly. The hand then takes out the wrapped food, which is revealed to be tonkatsu sandwiches. The scene transitions to two young girls in pajamas sitting at a wooden table, eating breakfast. The girl in blue pajamas has a half-eaten plate of food and a spoon, while the girl in green pajamas uses a fork to eat. An adult hand then serves more food from a white bowl onto the plate of the girl in blue pajamas, who then happily eats with her hands. Finally, the video shows a woman in a white long-sleeved shirt and blue jeans making a bed in a bedroom, shaking and arranging a white duvet and pillows on a bed with a wooden headboard.

The video opens at 0:04 showing two young children, likely toddlers, on a light wooden floor. The child on the left wears blue pajamas with cartoon characters and sits with their back mostly to the camera, surrounded by small, dark-packaged items. The child on the right wears colorful pajamas featuring candy patterns, stands and holds a small white cardboard box, actively pulling out more of the dark-packaged items. On-screen text reads, "How to keep your kids entertained when most of their toys are packed? Just give them some packets of food." At 0:11, the scene transitions to a woman with dark hair tied back, wearing a white speckled long-sleeved t-shirt. She is speaking directly to the camera, gesturing with her hands and smiling. Behind her, a bed with white bedding and a wooden wardrobe are visible. As she continues to speak and move slightly, the background changes to reveal a window with a balcony view, a wooden table, and a black bag on the floor, before showing a white wall with a control panel and a wooden door.

A woman with dark hair, wearing a white padded jacket with a fur-lined hood, is holding a baby dressed in a white fluffy hooded outfit with bear ears. The woman is speaking to the camera, smiling, and looking around, while the baby observes its surroundings, occasionally sticking out its tongue. They are on a bustling city street in Japan, with various people walking in the background. Behind them, several signs are visible; to the left, a yellow sign with red and green elements displays some Japanese text and illustrations of food, likely for a restaurant or shop. As the camera moves, a blue sign with white Japanese text "アパマン" (Apaman) and "入口" (Entrance) is seen, indicating an entrance to an Apaman real estate office. Further down the street, signs for "カラオケ" (Karaoke) and "サイゼリヤ" (Saizeriya), a family restaurant, are visible, along with a green bus and a crosswalk on the street.

The video opens with a woman wearing a white jacket with a fur-lined hood talking to someone off-camera, describing the area as a "hangout spot" where political announcements are made via a large microphone. Another woman in a plaid shirt and white tank top joins the conversation, elaborating on the political activity. The scene then shifts to two young girls, one in a purple jacket and the other in a white jacket, playing on a patterned gray pavement with tactile paving studs, running and interacting near a woman in black pants. The first woman reappears, continuing to talk to the camera, mentioning how busy the area was past midnight. The children continue to play, running back and forth, and one of them attempts to pick up a yellow sign with Japanese text (which translates to "No Smoking"). The video then shows a busy city street with cars, a green bus, and buildings, including one with a large yellow sign that reads "ドン・キホーテ" (Don Quijote). Finally, the woman in the white jacket is seen holding the little girl in the white jacket, both looking at the camera, while she continues to talk and smile.

The video opens on a tiled city sidewalk, where a man in a black athletic jacket and black shorts stands smiling and interacting with a small child in a pink outfit, who briefly runs into the frame. The child, now in a white jacket, approaches the man's leg. Subsequently, a woman in a white puffer jacket films herself while walking on the street with the child, who is later seen in a pink hoodie, entering a bustling Japanese discount store. Inside, the children explore the crowded aisles filled with diverse products, pointing out Mickey Mouse-themed lip balm and Star Wars-branded "UNO" shaving gel and face wash (one featuring R2-D2). The shelves showcase an array of aesthetically packaged laundry detergents and fabric softeners, including brands like "Aroma Rich" and "Landrin," and numerous hair dye products such as "Palty" and "Fresh Light," with boxes depicting Japanese women. A unique "Beauty labo" (ホイップ ヘアカラー - Hoippu Hea Kara, "Whip Hair Color") hair dye packaged like a milkshake is also spotted. The final scenes show the group of two women and two children gathered in a hallway with multiple suitcases and travel bags, including a "GRACO" pack-n-play, preparing to leave, before cutting to the woman holding a baby in a pink fluffy hoodie inside an elevator.

The video opens with a woman, wearing a white puffer jacket with a fur-lined hood, holding a baby with dark hair in a small ponytail, who is dressed in a pink fuzzy hooded jacket. They are in what appears to be an elevator or small room with light-colored walls; the woman smiles and talks to the camera while the baby transitions from a serious expression to a wide smile, laughing and raising her hand as if waving. The scene then cuts to the baby, now wearing a white hooded top over pink and blue pants, sitting in a car seat and contemplatively putting her finger in her mouth. The video transitions again to show a slightly older child, likely a toddler, with dark hair, wearing a purple jacket and blue jeans, also seated in a car seat, holding a colorful toy and looking towards the camera while talking and smiling briefly, with the car window revealing an outside view in the background.

A young girl with dark hair, wearing a bright purple long-sleeved top and blue jeans, is seated securely in a dark-colored car seat within a vehicle. She holds a small, orange and green plush toy on her lap, resting her hands on it. Her gaze is directed towards the left side of the frame, looking at the camera, with a neutral to slightly pensive expression. The car seat's harness straps are visible across her chest. To her left, a car window reveals a blurry outdoor background, suggesting movement or an external scene. At the end of the segment, she briefly opens her mouth as if speaking.

The video opens inside a vehicle, showing the back of two individuals in the front seats: a person in a maroon shirt with short dark hair in the passenger seat, looking right, and the driver, wearing glasses and dark clothing, partially visible behind the steering wheel. A digital screen is visible on the dashboard, and a laptop or tablet with an unreadable notification bubble is in the foreground, likely held by someone in the back. The scene then transitions to show a young child with dark hair, wearing a purple jacket and jeans, sitting securely in a car seat in the back of the vehicle, holding two orange objects in their lap and looking out the window at the buildings and street passing by.

The video opens with a child in a car seat, wearing a purple jacket and blue jeans with orange socks, looking out the window while occasionally moving their hands. Buildings and trees are visible outside the car, and a man's arm and shoulder are reflected in the window. The scene transitions to an indoor setting where three young children are seated at a wooden dining table, eating. A white cloth hangs to dry near a window, which overlooks a building with arched windows. Throughout this indoor scene, various comment boxes pop up: "AbbySaysHella 7 hours ago Next step is a palo, I'm telling you... -Benji LOL hear that everyday in a Filipino household" (AbbySaysHella humorously references a common Filipino saying about a 'palo' or stick); "Rocky Breeze 8 hours ago Will Miyako ever be able to do a successful handstand with out having a giggle fit? lol cutiebear ahaha" (Rocky Breeze asks if Miyako can do a handstand without giggling); "Juicyy George 9 hours ago auntie mel is so pretty 😍" (Juicyy George compliments 'auntie mel'); and "livinwitherika 1 hour ago Im going to miss Japan" (livinwitherika expresses sadness about leaving Japan). Small inset videos also appear in the bottom right corner, showing a baby eating with an adult, a close-up of a steak dish, a baby in a pink bow looking at the camera, a baby eating pizza and giving a thumbs-up, and another child sitting on and then running from a brown ottoman. The perspective then shifts to a "JB Cam" view, showing a close-up of a green plush toy and a red seatbelt buckle inside a car, followed by blurry glimpses of a purple object and the car's ceiling, before the screen turns completely black.
